I'm not an Rstan user. I'm doing tech support for Rstan want-to-be users.

Can one of you point me at code for an Rstan job that runs for a day or so and tests out a lot of the bells and whistles? One that does not crash at the end would be an extra good choice :)

Here's why I asked. On the cluster computing system here, they run RHEL 6. Old, I know.  We've been through a circus getting GCC-6.3 and all of the preliminaries for Stan built in a consistent way.  We are able now to compile and install the rstan R package, and a few small test jobs run well. Along the way to compile this, however, there are tons of g++ warnings and I'm not entirely confident about it.  I see the message in your web pages about silencing the g++ warnings, but that goes against my instinct. I found various advice in the STAN pages and lists about CXX flags in the Makevars file, but I found that rstan failed to compile if I fiddled around if I insert any optimizer flags.  I am not a GCC or compiler novice, but this is making me feel young again, like a beginner:)

The student who I've assigned to test this out has a Rstan job that takes 8 hours on her MS Windows computer, where it runs fine (I'm told, at least), but when she puts that in the cluster, it runs for about 22 hours and then has a crash that looks suspiciously like a g++ memory allocation error, which I paste in below.

There are many possible reasons for the crash, of course. R is 3.3 (from MRO, because that links to Intel MKL).  I need to get sessionInfo() output from the various systems to compare package versions. There may be a flaw in the user's job. There's some Rcpp magic floating about in there.  Plus, I've got old old OS sitting about, with GCC 6.3 which we have compiled ourselves, along with Boost, OpenMPI, and all of that other stuff. The other wild card is the memory limit on the cluster node, which we've set at 12GB, which we believe is about 2x what is truly necessary.  But, then again, if you tell me the crash below is due to memory shortage, I'll believe you.

I realize I need to get a detailed backtrace for the crash. If you think that's a top priority, I will try harder.   In the meanwhile, I ask you for a big STAN program I can run on a cluster node.  If your job fails too, it means my setup needs help.  If your job succeeds, well, suspect problem is in the user's code.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Got a big STAN test program? I have a bus error
parts:
On Wednesday, April 26, 2017 at 12:57:23 AM UTC-4, Paul Johnson wrote:
I'm not an Rstan user.
Can one of you point me at code for an Rstan job that runs for a day or so and tests out a lot of the bells and whistles? One that does not crash at the end would be an extra good choice :)

I don't think I have any interesting examples of long-running code that I can share, but we have definitely seen Stan run for days and come out fine in the end. You could try a simple Stan program without data like

transformed data {
  int K = 5000; // or other large integer
}
parameters {
  corr_matrix[K] Sigma;
}
model {}

The student who I've assigned to test this out has a Rstan job that takes 8 hours on her MS Windows computer, where it runs fine (I'm told, at least), but when she puts that in the cluster, it runs for about 22 hours and then has a crash that looks suspiciously like a g++ memory allocation error, which I paste in below.

That looks to me like either:
  • the Stan program got compiled on a worker node and when the stanfit object was passed back to the analysis node, the worker node shut down leaving a dangling pointer to the stanmodel object inside the stanfit object
  • an overly aggressive server script decided to delete the shared object in tempdir() because it wasn't touched for a certain number of hours

I think the first is more likely. The solution to that would involve compiling the thing on the analysis node with stan_model() and passing the resulting object to the worker nodes when you call sampling(). Server setups vary, but I know people have done Stan stuff on the Columbia clusters which also use torque.


Ben

I got to the bottom of this problem. The submission script did not have "--vanilla" in the R program call.  I always do that, as a matter of habit, because it eliminates usage of saved workspaces (.RData) or user profile and such. The student omitted that, and when we put it in, then the job stopped crashing.

Can a reasonable explanation be like this? The student used Rstan on a Windows system using the standard Rtools setup, which has older gcc than we have in the cluster.  This left behind .RData and an old session traveled to the cluster, where the special Windows magic was not compatible with the RHEL 6, gcc-6.3 version of Rstan. When R started, and loaded that workspace, there were some Windows-build rstan objects floating about.

I don't have access to carefully inspect the user's account, but it is also possible there is something untoward in .Rprofile.  I'm trying to find out.

It is a one node only, multiple core model.  No MPI issues are tied in.  I need to work out the MPI version next, because the multicore code takes about 1 day per MCMC chain, and the project is supposed to explore 1000s of these things.  I will post separate questions to get help on that.

This left me wondering about the Rstan customization of the Makevars file, how that is affected by "--vanilla".
Ben

On Thursday, May 4, 2017 at 9:11:23 AM UTC-4, Paul Johnson wrote:
Can a reasonable explanation be like this? The student used Rstan on a Windows system using the standard Rtools setup, which has older gcc than we have in the cluster.  This left behind .RData and an old session traveled to the cluster, where the special Windows magic was not compatible with the RHEL 6, gcc-6.3 version of Rstan. When R started, and loaded that workspace, there were some Windows-build rstan objects floating about.
That is entirely possible. In general, you can't mix stanfit or stanmodel objects from different operating systems or even from different versions of the compiler on the same operating system.
This left me wondering about the Rstan customization of the Makevars file, how that is affected by "--vanilla".

I think "not at all"

man R | grep -A 1 -F -- "--vanilla"

says it does not read sitewise Makevars files but it seems to not exclude users' Makevars files.

Ben
